## PM triage + dispatch order — R27. ⚠️ **Split card: the `body` row is dispatchable now; the unnamed-intersection half is a contract decision.**

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-6169-chatbot-body-row`.

Same split I applied to #6172 tonight, for the same reason: one half is a live false statement that needs no ruling, the other sets a cross-package contract that is not this seat's to set.

### ⭐ Dispatchable half: the `body` row documents a key that reaches nothing

The Properties table's `body` row reads *"Additional body params for API requests"*. That is **false as authoring guidance**:

- The node key that carries those params is **`requestBody`** — the renderer passes it as `body: schema.requestBody` (`renderer.tsx:87`), so `body` is the name of the *prop it becomes*, not the key an author writes.
- The `body` a reader would actually find on the node is **`BaseSchema.body`** — the children container. So an author following this row writes a real key with a completely unrelated meaning, and their API params silently reach nothing.

⭐ This is worse than a wrong name: `body` **exists** on the node. The reader gets no error, no unknown-key warning, and no signal — they get the children container quietly doing something else. A row naming a key that does not exist would at least fail loudly.

Fix the row to name `requestBody`, and describe it as the authored key rather than the prop it becomes. ⛔ Do not rename anything in source — `renderer.tsx:87` is correct as written; the table is what is wrong.

### What to verify before and after

1. **Re-measure at your claim SHA.** Confirm `renderer.tsx` still does `body: schema.requestBody`, confirm `ChatbotSchema` declares `requestBody`, and confirm `BaseSchema` declares `body` as the children container. ⭐ All three readings, not just the first — the card's claim is a *collision* between two real keys, so a single grep proves nothing.
2. Confirm `ChatbotSchema` declares **no** `body` of its own with the documented meaning, which is the specific claim the row gets wrong.
3. After the edit, confirm no other row on the page names `body` with the API-params meaning.

### ⛔ Out of scope — leave these alone and say so in the report

- **The 11 keys declared only at the registration site.** `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/renderer.tsx:62` types its node with an **inline, anonymous intersection**, so `showTimestamp`, `userAvatarUrl`, `userAvatarFallback`, `assistantAvatarUrl`, `assistantAvatarFallback`, `maxHeight`, `autoResponse`, `autoResponseText`, `autoResponseDelay`, `onSend` and `surface` are authorable surface with **no declaration anyone can import**. Whether the fix is to lift that extension into `ChatbotSchema` or to name and export it is a contract decision — escalated below, not yours.
- ⛔ **Do not "fix" the Properties table by deleting the 11 unbacked rows.** They are **not dead surface**: `autoResponse` / `autoResponseText` / `autoResponseDelay` are read by a live consumer at `packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx:1599-1601`. Deleting documentation for surface that actually works would be a regression dressed as a cleanup.
- ⛔ Do not add a "which type does this table describe?" sentence. #6086 stopped on this page precisely because **no single declared shape carries the 25 rows**, so any name you write would be false. That is the escalated half, and writing a name is pre-empting it.

### Verification

- Gate union with exit codes captured by redirect **before** any pipe, each quoting its own verdict line. ⚠️ **Derive the gate list from `package.json` and `.github/workflows/` rather than from this order** — my last order named `check:doc-snippet-types`, which is the script *file*; the npm script is `check:doc-snippets`, and re-deriving also surfaces `check:doc-fences`. Read the repo, not me.
- Measure each gate's inclusion or exclusion from its own configuration rather than asserting it.
- Root vitest only, per objectui#3378.
- Changeset per the presence gate's own verdict; objectui has no `skip-changeset` mechanism, so that verdict is the declaration form.
- ⚠️ Use **"Part of #6169"**, never a closing keyword — the card must survive its own PR because the escalated half stays open.

### ⛔ Escalated as `needs-user-decision`: the unnamed inline intersection

Eleven authorable keys of the `chatbot` node exist **only** inside an anonymous type at the registration site. Nothing outside that file can reference them, nothing can validate against them, and the docs page has no type to point a reader at — which is why #6086 could not name this table and filed instead.

⚠️ It is the same family as #6172's collision class (already escalated) and #6155 (held behind it), but it is a **different failure**: those are one name with several shapes; this is a **shape with no name at all**. Recording it separately so the decision covers both, and noting the sibling relationship so they are ruled together rather than twice.

## PM review — docs half ACCEPTED. PR #6193 armed. ⛔ The card stays OPEN for the escalated half.

Reviewed against a pinned ref. 20 checks green, 0 failures, 1 running.

### The fix says more than "rename the key", and that is right

The diff is **1 file, +2 / −2**. The table cell now reads:

> Additional body parameters sent with each API request. Authored on the node as `requestBody`; the renderer forwards it to the chat runtime under its own `body` option. **Writing `body` on the node instead sets the base schema's children container and never reaches the API.**

⭐ That last clause is what the card was actually about, and I did not ask for it. The defect was never "the key has the wrong name" — it was that `body` **exists** on the node as something else, so an author following the old row got no error, no unknown-key warning, and their API params silently went to the children container. Naming `requestBody` alone would have fixed the row while leaving the trap unmarked for anyone who had already written `body`. Stating the collision is the difference between a corrected row and a row that prevents the mistake.

It also correctly distinguishes the **authored key** from the **prop it becomes**, which is the distinction that made the original row wrong.

### ⚠️ One extension beyond my stated scope — ratifying it, and saying why

My order scoped this to the Properties table row. The diff also changes the **`## Schema API` block at line 110**, which declared the identical false `body` key for the same authored node.

I am accepting it, and it is not creep: my own order required *"after the edit, confirm no other row on the page names `body` with the API-params meaning"* — that mandated check is exactly what surfaced it. Shipping a PR that fixed the table while the same false declaration survived **one screen above, in the block a reader meets first**, would have been worse than not touching the page. Only that one key was changed in the block.

This is the second time tonight a dev extended a docs fix by one hunk because leaving it would have shipped a known-false statement (#6160 did the same with `ci-cd-pipeline.md`). Both were right. I should scope docs orders as "the false statement and its duplicates" rather than naming one site.

### The five-point pre-edit verification is the standard I want

Every leg of the collision claim measured before touching anything, not inferred from the card:

1. `renderer.tsx` still does `body: schema.requestBody` — at **three** sites (87, 305, 438), not the one the card named.
2. `ChatbotSchema` declares `requestBody`, doc-commented as the API-request params.
3. `BaseSchema` declares `body` at `base.ts:121` as *"Child components or content"* — the children container.
4. ⭐ A grep for a `body` key **inside the `ChatbotSchema` interface block** matches **zero** times. That is the negative leg, and it is the one that makes the collision claim a reading rather than an assumption.
5. After the edit, the page's only remaining `body` occurrences are the table cell naming it **to warn against it**, and a `fetch()` option inside an `onSend` example — which is the Fetch API's own `body` and is correct.

Point 5 matters: a careless sweep would have "fixed" that `fetch()` call and broken a working example.

⭐ And gate inclusion was measured, producing **two independent reasons** the snippet gate cannot move: the page is among its 44 `UNGATED_DOCS`, *and* the edited line sits inside a `plaintext` fence. Two reasons where one would do is the right instinct — if the first turns out wrong, the conclusion survives.

Edits applied by exact-literal replacement with anchor counts asserted **before** the write (row=1, fence=1, abort otherwise) and re-grepped after. An editor's exit code was not treated as evidence of a hit — the trap that has bitten twice tonight.

### Scope held on everything that mattered

⛔ No source change — `renderer.tsx` is correct. ⛔ The 11 unbacked rows were **not** deleted, correctly: `autoResponse` / `autoResponseText` / `autoResponseDelay` have a live consumer at `AiChatPage.tsx:1599-1601`, so deleting them would have been a regression dressed as a cleanup. ⛔ No "which type does this table describe" sentence was added — #6086 stopped on this page precisely because no declared shape carries the 25 rows, and writing a name would have pre-empted the escalated decision.

**"Part of #6169"**, no closing keyword, so the card survives its own PR.

The duplicated signature footer the platform appended was left alone rather than edited — the right call, since editing the body risks the footer-strip path for no benefit.

### Still open

⛔ The **unnamed inline intersection** at `renderer.tsx:62` — 11 authorable keys with no declaration anyone can import. That is now grouped with #6172, #6155 and #6170 as **one family with one decision**: the authoring surface and the exported type disagree, and `BaseSchema`'s index signature means nothing mechanical notices. See the synthesis on #6170. ⛔ None of the contract halves should be dispatched until the family is ruled together.

## ⛔ State correction — the dispatchable half has LANDED; what remains is the escalated half

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_01Mn4BZ5AVDM81pvfij1WwM9` (`os-litant`).

This card was split by the `domain:devx` seat: one half dispatchable now, one half a cross-package contract decision. **The dispatchable half is finished and merged.** The card has nevertheless been sitting in `pm:queue`, which reads to any lane sweep as *ready to dispatch* — so the next seat to scan this lane would have re-dispatched work that is already on `main`.

### Verified on `origin/main`, by content and not by commit message

| leg | reading |
|---|---|
| merged commit | `ead74abe4` — *"docs(plugin-chatbot): name the authored key as `requestBody`, not `body` (#6193)"* |
| branch `claude/issue-6169-chatbot-body-row` | **gone** (deleted after squash merge) |
| content probe | `git grep -c requestBody origin/main -- content/docs/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx` → **2** |

⚠️ The content probe is the load-bearing one. This repo **squash-merges** and deletes the branch, so an absent branch is compatible with *both* "merged" and "abandoned" — ⛔ a missing branch alone proves nothing. The two legs together settle it.

**This stroke:** `pm:queue` → `needs-user-decision`, for the half that actually remains.

### What remains, and why it is not this seat's

The escalated half is the **unnamed inline intersection** that forms the `chatbot` authoring surface. Per the routing seat, that half *"sets a cross-package contract that is not this seat's to set"* — naming and exporting an authoring type is a **published surface** question, which is the manual floor by the mechanical boundary test. **No ruling has been posted on it.**

✅ Worth preserving from the review of the landed half, because it is the standard this lane wants: the fix did **more** than rename the key. The final cell says not only that the authored key is `requestBody`, but that **writing `body` instead silently sets the base schema's children container and never reaches the API**. The defect was never "the key has the wrong name" — it was that `body` **exists on the node as something else**, so an author following the old row got no error, no unknown-key warning, and their API params vanished into the children container. ⭐ Naming the *silent* failure, not just the correct spelling, is what made that a real fix.

Dispatching the **escalated half only**, on the maintainer's 2026-08-25 ruling (06:47Z, confirmed 10:14Z — 「上午的批量是我决裁的。」). Recording what a reader of this thread needs, because it has been through a split, a landing, and two state corrections in opposite directions.

## ⛔ The docs half is DONE — do not redo it

PR #6193 merged as `ead74abe4`; the Properties table and the `## Schema API` block both name `requestBody` now. This dispatch touches **no documentation** except what the new type makes newly nameable. ⛔ Do not re-verify the `body` / `requestBody` collision and do not re-edit that page's table rows.

⚠️ Note for the dev on how that was confirmed, because it is the reusable part: this repo **squash-merges and deletes the branch**, so an absent branch is compatible with both "merged" and "abandoned" — ⛔ a missing branch alone proves nothing. The load-bearing leg was a **content probe on `origin/main`**, not the commit message.

## The ruling, and the one clause that shapes the work

> lift the 11-key anonymous inline intersection at `renderer.tsx:62` into a named, exported declaration (extend `ChatbotSchema` or a named exported extension type — **implementer's structural call**), so the keys become referenceable, validatable, and documentable

⭐ And the clause that makes this more than a rename:

> each remaining key gets a **read-site check on the way in** — a key with **zero read points anywhere** goes the **ADR-0049 route** instead of getting immortalized

So this is not "wrap the existing 11 in a name." It is a per-key census, and the census decides which keys the new type declares. `autoResponse` / `autoResponseText` / `autoResponseDelay` are **definitely in** — measured live consumer at `packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx:1599-1601`. Every other key must earn its place with a read site or take the retirement route.

⚠️ **Re-measure the key list itself.** The card says 11 and separately names `surface`; the inline intersection as quoted also carries `disabled`, which the registration destructures separately. Those do not obviously reconcile, and the card is from 2026-08-24. Derive the set from the tree, report what you find, and ⛔ do not implement from the card's list.

## ⛔ If any key takes the ADR-0049 route, DELETION IS NOT REFUSAL

This lane's most expensive shape, met five times: under `.passthrough()` or an index signature, **removing a key does not refuse it — it stops judging it and keeps it.** `BaseSchema` has an index signature, which is precisely why nothing mechanical notices this disagreement today. A retired key therefore needs a **declared** refusal (a `?: never` + `z.never().optional()` tombstone on both halves in lockstep), never a quiet deletion.

## Clause-② — contract-review tier

The ruling says so explicitly: **yes**, this changes published type surface. Per this lane's standing order clause-② goes **at-tier, straight to the queue**, which is why it is dispatched rather than escalated again. ⛔ `needs:contract-review` is a phantom label in this repo with zero readers — do not apply it; the tier is carried by the review, not by a label.

## Fences and the serial constraint

- ⚠️ **`packages/types` is shared right now.** The #6424 remainder dispatch holds `packages/types/src/data-display.ts` (column keys) and `packages/plugin-grid`. Your surface is `packages/types/src/complex.ts` (`ChatbotSchema`) and `packages/plugin-chatbot` — different files, so this is not a block. **The one real collision point is `packages/types/src/index.ts`** if you add a barrel export. Keep that edit to the single line you need, and say in your report that you touched it.
- ⚠️ The ruling says *"coordinate serially with the #6172 family claim if one seat takes both."* **#6172 is unassigned and not in flight**, so there is no live claim to coordinate with — but ⛔ do not extend into `FormField` / `MarkdownSchema` / `KanbanSchema`. They are #6172's, and this card is one member of the family, not the family.
- ⛔ `renderer.tsx:87` is correct as written. The defect is the anonymous type, not the forwarding.

## Why the card is worth doing at all

Eleven authorable keys of a shipped node exist **only** inside an anonymous type at a registration site. Nothing outside that file can reference them, nothing can validate against them, and the docs page has no type to point a reader at — which is why #6086 stopped here and filed rather than naming something false. This is the *shape-with-no-name* member of the family; #6172's is *one name with several shapes*.
